pageCache.pageTitle: Sarum St Paul's CofE (VA) Primary School - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values at Sarum St Paul's
At Sarum St Paul's, we are committed to preparing our children to be thoughtful, responsible and active citizens. Through our vision, Rooted in Love, Growing Together, we nurture children who understand their place in the wider world and who are ready to make a positive contribution to society.
The Department for Education states that all schools should actively promote the fundamental British Values of:
These values are embedded throughout school life and are closely linked to our Christian vision and values of Love, Community, Courage and Growth.
Democracy
The Rule of Law
Individual Liberty
Mutual Respect
Democracy
We encourage children to understand that their voice matters and that everyone has the right to be heard.
Children experience democracy through:
Through these experiences, children learn that decisions can be made fairly and that everyone has a role to play within a community.
School Council elections and pupil leadership opportunities
Learning to listen respectfully to different opinions
The Rule of Law
Children learn the importance of rules and why they help keep everyone safe, happy and able to learn.
We promote this through:
Children learn that rules and laws exist to protect individuals and communities.
Our school rules: Ready, Respectful, Safe
Consistent behaviour expectations and restorative approaches
Learning about rights and responsibilities
Individual Liberty
We encourage children to make choices, take responsibility and develop confidence in who they are.
Children are given opportunities to:
We help children understand that freedom comes with responsibility and respect for the rights of others.
Take on leadership roles and responsibilities
Express their views respectfully
Develop resilience and independence
Mutual Respect
Respect lies at the heart of our school community and reflects our Christian vision of being rooted in love.
Our diverse school community provides many opportunities for children to learn the importance of positive relationships and belonging.
Treat others with kindness and consideration
Value the contributions of others
Work collaboratively and support one another
Celebrate each other's achievements
Tolerance of Different Faiths and Beliefs
As a Church of England school, we celebrate diversity and encourage children to develop an understanding of different faiths, beliefs and cultures.
This is promoted through:
We encourage children to be curious, respectful and open-minded, recognising that every person is unique and valued.
Religious Education
Collective worship
Learning about different cultures and traditions
Marking significant festivals and events
Welcoming visitors from different backgrounds and communities
Living British Values Every Day
British Values are not taught as a standalone subject. They are woven through our curriculum, collective worship, relationships and daily interactions.
By living out our vision, Rooted in Love, Growing Together, we help our children develop into confident, respectful and compassionate citizens who are ready to contribute positively to their local, national and global communities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sarum St Paul's CofE (VA) Primary School - Church Inspection (SIAMS)
pageCache.text:
Church Inspection (SIAMS)
As a Church of England Primary School, we are inspected through the Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS). While Ofsted evaluates the overall quality of education, SIAMS considers how effectively our Christian vision shapes every aspect of school life and enables children and adults to flourish.
At Sarum St Paul's, our vision, Rooted in Love, Growing Together, is at the heart of everything we do. Inspired by the words of St Paul in Ephesians 3:17-18, we seek to create a school community where every child and adult is rooted in God's love, grows in confidence and character and is encouraged to flourish academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually.
What Does SIAMS Look At?
SIAMS explores how our Christian vision is lived out across the whole school community, including:
The impact of our vision on the wellbeing and flourishing of pupils, staff and the wider community.
The quality of collective worship and opportunities for spiritual development.
The effectiveness of Religious Education.
How we create an inclusive culture where every individual is known, valued and respected.
How our vision inspires courageous advocacy, service and responsibility towards others.
Rather than focusing solely on outcomes, SIAMS considers how the school's Christian foundation influences decisions, relationships and the daily experiences of everyone within our community.
Living Our Vision Every Day
Our Christian vision is not simply a statement on a wall. It shapes the way we learn, the way we care for one another and the decisions we make each day.
Across our school you will see our vision reflected through:
A welcoming and inclusive community where every child is known and valued.
A broad and ambitious curriculum that enables every child to achieve their potential.
Collective worship that encourages reflection, prayer and spiritual growth.
Strong relationships built on kindness, respect and forgiveness.
Opportunities for children to develop leadership, responsibility and serve others.
A commitment to supporting the wellbeing of every member of our school community.
Our SIAMS Inspection
Our most recent SIAMS inspection took place in 2019, when the school was judged to be Excellent.
We are proud of this recognition and continue to build on these strengths as we develop our school and live out our Christian vision each day.
Read our latest SIAMS report
Discover More
If you would like to learn more about our Christian distinctiveness, we invite you to explore the following pages:

pageCache.pageTitle: Sarum St Paul's CofE (VA) Primary School - Our Vision amp Values
pageCache.text:
Our Vision & Values
Rooted in Love, Growing Together
At Sarum St Paul's Church of England Primary School, everything we do is inspired by our vision:
Rooted in Love, Growing Together
Our vision is based on a prayer written by St Paul to the Christians in Ephesus:
"And I pray that you, being rooted and grounded in love, may have power, together with all the Lord's holy people, to grasp how wide and long and high and deep is the love of Christ."(Ephesians 3:17-18)
Our vision is inspired by this prayer from St Paul to the Christians in Ephesus. Through it, we are reminded that when we are rooted and grounded in love, we can grow, flourish and achieve more together than any of us could alone.
At the heart of this prayer is the image of being rooted and grounded in love. Just as a tree needs strong roots to grow and flourish, we believe that people thrive when they are nurtured within a community built on love, care and belonging.
Our vision is for every member of our school community. We want our children, staff, governors, families and wider community to feel valued, supported and empowered to flourish. By being rooted in love, we create the strong foundations that enable us to grow together, learn from one another and become the very best versions of ourselves.
Our four values of Love, Community, Courage and Growth help us to live out this vision every day.
Love: Our Roots
Love is the root from which our vision grows and the foundation of everything we do.
Jesus taught that love is not simply something we feel. Love is something we do. Through kindness, compassion, forgiveness and care for others, we put love into action every day.
To help our children understand this value, we explore the story of the Good Samaritan. Through this story, children learn that love means noticing others, showing compassion and taking action when someone needs our help.
When we are rooted in love, we help ourselves, others and our whole community to flourish.
Community: Growing Together
We believe that everyone belongs and everyone has something valuable to contribute.
At Sarum St Paul's, we celebrate our differences and recognise that we are stronger when we work together. We encourage children to support one another, value different perspectives and understand that each person plays an important role in our school family.
This value is brought to life through Paul's teaching of One Body, Many Parts. Children learn that just as each part of the body has a different purpose, every person has unique gifts and strengths that help our community thrive.
By growing together, we create a community where everyone feels seen, valued and included.
Courage: Reaching Beyond What We Thought Possible
Courage helps us to face challenges, persevere through difficulties and stand up for what is right.
We encourage our children to be brave in their learning, resilient when things are difficult and confident enough to try something new. Courage helps us to step outside our comfort zone and keep going when things feel challenging.
To explore this value, we reflect on the story of David and Goliath. Through David's determination and trust in God, children see that courage is not about being the biggest or strongest, but about finding the confidence to face challenges and do what is right.
Growth: Flourishing and Bearing Fruit
Growth is at the heart of learning and becoming the best version of ourselves.
At Sarum St Paul's, we nurture growth academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually. We encourage children to embrace challenges, learn from mistakes and recognise that growth takes time.
This value is explored through The Parable of the Sower. Children learn that, just as seeds need the right conditions in which to grow, people flourish when they are nurtured, encouraged and given opportunities to develop their gifts and talents.
We believe that every member of our community has the potential to flourish and make a positive contribution to the world around them.
Living Our Vision
Our vision and values are woven through every aspect of school life. They shape our learning, guide our relationships and inspire the way we care for one another.
For our children, the vision helps them to understand how they can learn, grow and contribute positively to the world around them. For staff, governors and leaders, it provides a framework for decision-making and school improvement. Whether we are planning the curriculum, developing opportunities for pupils, supporting families or setting the strategic direction of the school, we seek to ensure that our choices reflect our vision and values.
Our vision acts as a compass for decision-making. We regularly ask ourselves how our choices will help our community to be more deeply rooted in love and enable every member of our community to grow and flourish. This ensures that our Christian vision is not simply a statement, but something that actively shapes the life and direction of our school.
Through Love, Community, Courage and Growth, we strive to create a school where every member of the community feels known, valued and supported to flourish.
Rooted in Love, Growing Together.
Diary Dates
Latest News

pageCache.pageTitle: Sarum St Paul's CofE (VA) Primary School - St Paul's Church
pageCache.text:
St Paul's Church
St Paul’s Church and Sarum St Paul’s School have enjoyed a close and supportive partnership for many years. We share a simple aim: to see every child, every member of staff, and every family flourish — not only academically, but spiritually, emotionally and socially.
As the local parish church, we are actively involved in the life of the school. Several members of our congregation — including me — serve as Governors, work on the school staff team, or have children at the school. If you are part of the school community, we already see you as part of our wider church family.
Each week, a member of our church team leads Collective Worship linked to the school’s curriculum. We love being welcomed into school, and it is always a privilege to host key events in our church building, such as the Year 6 Leavers’ Celebration and services for major Christian festivals. The children play a central role in these occasions, and their creativity and confidence always shine.
St Paul’s Church is a lively, friendly and contemporary place to worship, with excellent children’s and youth programmes. Our main Service is on Sunday at 10.30am. If you are curious about the Christian faith, we offer a range of short courses and resources — including Alpha, which we have run for over 20 years and which has helped millions of people worldwide explore life, faith and meaning.
For families with younger children, our Ark Toddler Group meets every Wednesday morning in the church and provides a warm, welcoming space for parents, carers and little ones. In our community centre, The Hope Centre, located at 159–161 Fisherton Street, we partner with Imagine This, a Family Hub offering support for early years development, special educational needs, mother‑and‑baby care, and opportunities to connect with other families.
We are also home to Salisbury Foodbank on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, and we work closely with Christians Against Poverty (CAP), a national charity offering free, confidential debt advice.
If you would like to know more about St Paul’s Church, or if we can support you in any way, we would be delighted to hear from you. We look forward to welcoming your family to Sarum St Paul’s School and are confident that your child will thrive and flourish as they learn and grow during their time here.
Diary Dates

pageCache.pageTitle: Sarum St Paul's CofE (VA) Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Sarum St Paul's Church of England Primary School
It is my absolute privilege to welcome you to Sarum St Paul's CE Primary School.
At Sarum St Paul's, we believe that every child is unique, valued and capable of achieving great things. As a Church of England school, our vision is to be "Rooted in Love, Growing Together", inspired by the words of St Paul in Ephesians 3:17-19. This vision sits at the heart of everything we do and shapes our relationships, our learning and our aspirations for every member of our school community.
We are proud to be a warm, inclusive and nurturing school where children are encouraged to be curious, courageous and compassionate. Through our values of Love, Community, Courage and Growth, we help children develop not only as learners but also as kind and responsible individuals who are ready to make a positive difference in the world around them.
Our dedicated staff work hard to create an environment where children feel safe, supported and challenged. We have high expectations for all our pupils and are committed to providing a rich and engaging curriculum that inspires a love of learning and enables every child to flourish academically, socially and spiritually.
Strong relationships are at the heart of our school. We value the partnership between home, school, church and the wider community, recognising that children thrive when we work together. We are proud of our welcoming and supportive school family and the sense of belonging that this creates for our children and their families.
Whether you are a prospective parent considering Sarum St Paul's for your child or a current member of our school community, I hope our website gives you a glimpse of the special place that our school is. Visitors often comment on the warmth, kindness and enthusiasm of our children and I would encourage you to come and see our school in action for yourself.
Thank you for taking the time to visit our website. We look forward to welcoming you to Sarum St Paul's and sharing in your child's journey.
Hannah EasthopeHeadteacher
Diary Dates

pageCache.text:
Extra-Curricular Clubs
Summer Term 2025/26
Club Registration Information
Pupils are invited to sign up for extra-curricular clubs on a termly basis (Autumn, Spring and Summer terms). At the start of each term, parents will receive a Google Form to register their child's interest in the available clubs.
Places are allocated at the beginning of the term, and parents will be notified by text message if their child has secured a place. If a club is oversubscribed and your child is not offered a place, they will be added to a waiting list and automatically enrolled for the following term.
Some clubs may incur a small charge; where applicable, this will be clearly communicated before the sign-up process opens. Payments can be made conveniently via School Money.
In the event that a club has to be cancelled due to adverse weather conditions, parents will be notified by text message no later than 2:00pm on the day of the club.
For further information please e-mail the school office on office@sarum-st-pauls.wilts.sch.uk or call 01722 336459

Breakfast and After School Clubs
Breakfast Club
In the mornings, Breakfast Club offers a calm and relaxed start, where children can enjoy a healthy breakfast, spend time with friends, and ease into the day through quiet activities, with opportunities to gently let off a little energy before school begins. This helps children feel settled and ready for a positive start to learning.
After School Club
After school, children can enjoy a wider mix of activities, including outdoor play and physical activity, alongside more relaxed options such as Lego, games and arts and crafts. This balanced approach allows children to unwind, be active, and choose how they want to end their day.
Other Information
Safe, registered and trusted
PH ActiveEd is an Ofsted-registered childcare provider. All staff hold an enhanced DBS, paediatric first aid and safeguarding training as a minimum, and each setting has its own risk assessment in place.
Because PH ActiveEd is Ofsted registered, you can pay using Tax-Free Childcare and childcare vouchers, as well as by card.
Times, prices and full details: please see the flyer below for session times, prices and what is included.

Outdoor Learning and Forest School
Learning Beyond the Classroom
At Sarum St Paul's, we believe that some of the most memorable learning happens outdoors.
Our school grounds and Forest School area provide children with regular opportunities to explore, discover and learn through hands-on experiences in nature. Led by our qualified Forest School Practitioner, our outdoor learning programme incorporates Forest School principles and is an important part of life at our school. It reflects our vision of Rooted in Love, Growing Together, helping children to develop confidence, resilience, curiosity and an appreciation of the natural world.
Whether children are investigating minibeasts, building shelters, creating natural artwork or simply taking time to notice the changing seasons, every session encourages children to learn through exploration, challenge and reflection.
Did You Know?
🌿 Every child enjoys regular outdoor learning as part of their time at Sarum St Paul's.
🌳 From September, Reception children will take part in outdoor learning every week, with sessions based on Forest School principles as a key part of their Early Years curriculum.
🍃 Sessions are led by a qualified Forest School Practitioner and supported by members of our teaching assistant team.
🍂 Learning takes place in almost all weather conditions. With suitable clothing, children discover that every season brings exciting new opportunities to learn and explore.
🔬 Outdoor learning plays an important role in supporting our Science curriculum, giving children first-hand opportunities to observe, investigate and explore the natural world.
💚 Outdoor learning helps children develop confidence, resilience, independence and a lifelong appreciation of the natural world.
Why Outdoor Learning Matters
Spending time outdoors supports children's development in many different ways. Through regular sessions, children develop:
confidence and resilience by taking on new challenges
independence, creativity and problem-solving skills
teamwork, communication and language skills
an appreciation of nature and the environment
positive mental health and emotional wellbeing
respect for themselves, others and God's creation
opportunities to apply and deepen classroom learning in meaningful ways.
Outdoor learning provides valuable opportunities to reinforce learning across the curriculum, particularly in Science, where children can observe seasonal change, explore habitats, identify plants and animals, investigate materials and develop scientific enquiry skills through real-life experiences. It also enriches learning in other areas of the curriculum.
What Happens During a Session?
Every session is carefully planned whilst remaining flexible enough to follow children's interests, the changing seasons and opportunities that arise through classroom learning. Activities may include:
den and shelter building
bug hunting and habitat exploration
nature identification
creating artwork using natural materials
scavenger hunts and nature trails
outdoor games and physical challenges
storytelling and imaginative play
teamwork and problem-solving activities
quiet reflection and mindfulness in nature.
Sessions are practical, active and child-centred, encouraging children to explore, investigate and work together.
Learning in Every Season
Outdoor learning takes place throughout the year and in almost all weather conditions. Children soon learn that every season brings something different, from searching for signs of spring and collecting autumn treasures to exploring mud, frost and puddles during the winter months.
We encourage children to embrace the outdoors safely and confidently by wearing suitable clothing for the weather. All children must have wellies to take part at all times of the year.
A Place to Grow
Outdoor learning is about far more than spending time outside. By incorporating Forest School principles, children become confident, resilient young people who are willing to have a go, work together, solve problems and care for the world around them.
These experiences support children's academic learning while also nurturing their social, emotional and spiritual development. By spending time in nature, children learn to be curious, respectful and reflective, developing skills and attitudes that will benefit them throughout their lives.
'Forest School makes us feel happy and calm. Nature is a very beautiful place.'
'I love that you can learn new things!'
'It's good, I REALLY enjoy it!'
When we do Forest School we learn how much we should appreciate nature.'
'I like it because you can express yourself.'
'We know how to look after the environment and be more careful around birds and animals'.

Our Governors
Welcome from the Chair
Sarum St Paul's is a thriving and welcoming school, where children are encouraged to flourish academically, socially and spiritually.
We are proud to be an Ofsted Good school, with Outstanding recognised in Personal Development (2024), reflecting our commitment to providing an inclusive education where every child is known, valued and supported to achieve their very best.
Our Christian vision, Rooted in Love, Growing Together, is at the heart of everything we do. Inspired by St Paul's words in Ephesians, it shapes our relationships, decision-making and aspirations for every member of our school community. We warmly welcome families of all faiths and those of none, creating a community where everyone is treated with dignity, kindness and respect.
The governing body works closely with our Headteacher, Mrs Hannah Easthope, and the leadership team to provide strategic leadership and ensure the school continues to thrive. Our role is to support and challenge school leaders, helping to ensure that every child receives the highest quality education and care.
Our governors come from a range of backgrounds, including parents, the Church, staff and the wider community. Together, we bring a wealth of experience and expertise, united by a shared commitment to helping the school achieve the very best for its children.
As governors, we help shape the school's long-term vision and strategic direction. We oversee the school's finances, monitor educational standards, hold leaders to account for the quality of education and the wellbeing of pupils and staff, and ensure that our resources are used effectively to benefit all children.
We are incredibly fortunate to have a dedicated and talented staff team who work tirelessly to help every child flourish. They create an environment where children feel safe, valued and inspired to develop a lifelong love of learning.
We are equally grateful for the support of our parents, carers and the wider school community. Whether volunteering in school, supporting educational visits, fundraising through Friends of Sarum St Paul's or encouraging learning at home, your partnership makes a tremendous difference to the life of our school.
I hope you enjoy exploring our website and learning more about our school and governing body. If you would like to find out more about our work or are interested in becoming involved in school governance in the future, please do get in touch.
